Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the biggest decision: whether FinSecure needs Private (VPC/on-prem) vs Dedicated capacity vs Hosted API. From our call I captured the following high-level requirements: 

- Strong data isolation: no customer data (inputs/outputs/telemetry) may be accessible outside your VPC or by multi-tenant control planes without explicit agreement.
- KMS/HSM integration for customer-managed keys.
- Audit logs and retention controls for tokens & payloads.
- SOC 2 + possibility of additional evidence for procurement.
- Timeline: ideally live for internal pilot by end of Q1 2027.

Based on that, short answers and asks: 
1) Do you consider "Dedicated" (customer-dedicated GPU pools with Redwood-managed control plane) acceptable if we can guarantee no data persistence outside your region and provide configuration to disable telemetry? Or do you require Private (customer-managed VPC or on-prem) where the control plane is in your network?
2) Who on your infra/security side should we loop in for a short architecture session (networking & KMS)?
3) Any procurement packet requirements we should prep now (e.g., sample contract clauses, insurance thresholds)?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share a one-pager comparing Dedicated vs Private VPC and a draft list of evidence items we can supply (SOC 2 report, architecture diagram, KMS integration steps).
- Schedule architecture call with your infra/security lead (30–45m).
- If Private is required, we’ll put together a high-level timeline and required on-prem/integration work.

I’ve attached the security questionnaire you mentioned (we’ll also send a redwood one-pager that outlines the difference between Dedicated and Private).

Best,

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and for the clear options. A few clarifications from the security side (copied our security alias):

- Data isolation is a hard requirement. We cannot allow model inputs/outputs or any plaintext telemetry to egress to a multi-tenant environment outside of FinSecure-managed infrastructure.
- Customer-managed KMS is required for keys that encrypt any persisted data; for in-transit we can use TLS but at-rest keys must be under our control.
- Audit logs must include request IDs, timestamps, and user identifiers; retention policy: minimum 1 year.
- We will need SOC 2 Type II and a security questionnaire answered (attached).

Given that, our preference is Private VPC (or on-prem) unless you can guarantee Dedicated will provide the same guarantees (control-plane isolation, no telemetry). What we care about most is the assurance that telemetry/inputs do not go to shared services and that keys & logs are under FinSecure control.

We’ve attached our security requirements PDF and a short checklist. Our infra lead, Priya Natarajan (priya.natarajan@finsecure.com), will own the architecture call. She’s available week of Nov 15.

Alex

Alex / Priya / Security team —

Thanks for the detail and the attached requirements. Quick clarifying notes and how we usually map these to deployment modes: 

- Hosted API: not suitable given your isolation/KMS needs (multi-tenant control plane and telemetry).

- Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated): provides dedicated GPU pools and tenant isolation at the serving layer. Control plane is still Redwood-hosted by default, but we can: 
  - Disable nonessential telemetry and provide a written telemetry policy.
  - Offer region lock and strict access controls.
  - Provide SOC 2 Type II and additional evidence (network traffic diagrams, pen test summary).
  However, Dedicated usually still has Redwood-managed control plane components (billing, monitoring). For some customers this is acceptable when contractually restricted; for others it is not.

- Private (VPC / on-prem): places either the control plane in your VPC or the entire stack on-prem. This ensures keys, logs, and network egress remain under your control. Private is the stronger guarantee for "no telemetry outside your network."

Recommended next steps:
1) Architecture call with Priya + our infra lead (Rishi) and Sean (SLA/contracts). We’ll walk network connectivity, KMS options (Cloud KMS/HSM patterns), and audit log delivery.
2) We’ll share a one-pager and a short checklist mapping which items we can cover in Dedicated vs Private.
3) If you prefer Private, we’ll prepare a high-level project plan and estimate for procurement.

Estimated timelines (very high level):
- Dedicated (contract + dedicated capacity): ~4–6 weeks after legal/PO, less integration work.
- Private VPC (customer-managed control plane): ~8–12 weeks (networking, KMS integration, audit hookup), depending on your infra availability.

I’ve attached the Redwood one-pager comparing both options and a sample network diagram.

Would next week (Nov 15–19) work for a 45m architecture session? I’ll send a Calendly link — feel free to propose a slot.

Best,
